subject: Request for credit: duplicated synthetic sessions driving usage spike
messages:
From: Priya Shah <priya@fastretail.com>
To: markus.klein@redwood.ai
Cc: FastRetail Finance <finance@fastretail.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Unexpected usage spike flagged as synthetic sessions — request for credit

Hi Markus,

We're seeing a large unexplained spike on our February invoice that the ops team flagged as 'synthetic/duplicate sessions' in your usage export. Attached is a brief snapshot (fastretail-usage-snapshot.zip) with the hour-by-hour counters.

Highlights:
- The spike starts 2027-02-08 03:00 UTC and peaks 2027-02-09 10:00 UTC.
- Our ingestion shows many identical session_ids and replayed requests (same prompt hashes) that look like they were re-ingested.
- Estimated incremental token count: ~1.1M tokens for Feb 8–9 (we're still vetting).

This is hitting our post-pay invoice and will push us over a credit threshold. Can Redwood confirm whether those sessions are billable duplicates or if you can issue a provisional credit while we investigate? We need a response before our finance cut on Feb 16.

Thanks — appreciate quick help here.

Priya Shah
Director, Platform Ops
FastRetail
priya@fastretail.com
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@fastretail.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 10 Feb 2027 10:45:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike flagged as synthetic sessions — request for credit

Hi Priya — thanks for the heads up and for the snapshot.

We're sorry to see that — I looped in Ben from Billing so we can triage consumption quickly. Can you send a short sample of the duplicated session_ids (5–10) and the time-window you want us to prioritize? If you prefer, we can accept the zip you attached and pull samples ourselves — just confirm which timezone the logs use.

Next steps from our side:
- Ben will run an initial duplicate-detection audit and provide provisional token counts.
- Engineering (cc'ed) will evaluate whether there was an ingestion or replay issue on Redwood's side.
- If we confirm internal duplication, we can provisionally issue a credit and follow up with a final reconciliation.

I appreciate the deadline—we'll aim to get a preliminary answer within 48 hours.

Best,
Markus Klein
Head of Customer Success – Billing & Revenue
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.ai
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@fastretail.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 12 Feb 2027 14:20:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike flagged as synthetic sessions — request for credit

Hi Priya — quick audit update. Thanks for the sample zip; I extracted a 1-hour window and ran our duplicate-detect. Summary below.

What we found (preliminary):
- Sample window: 2027-02-08T03:00:00Z — 2027-02-08T04:00:00Z
- Duplicate session_ids detected: 18,452 unique session_ids with 2+ occurrences in the window.
- Estimated extra tokens attributable to duplicates in the full Feb 8–9 window: ~1,230,000 tokens.
- Per your plan's rates, that maps to a provisional overcharge of $1,450.

Attachments: markus-session-sample-20270210.csv (sample rows and counts).

This is a provisional figure pending engineering confirmation of origin (client replays vs. platform re-ingest). Neha — can you confirm whether any backfill/replayer jobs or ingestion changes occurred in that timeframe? If it's on our side we'll propose a credit note for the full amount and adjust the Feb invoice prior to your finance cutoff.

Priya — want me to provision a temporary hold on invoice payment while we finalize? We can also issue an interim credit to prevent late payment exposure.

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.ai
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Shah <priya@fastretail.com>
Cc: markus.klein@redwood.ai, ben.carter@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 15 Feb 2027 14:36:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Unexpected usage spike flagged as synthetic sessions — request for credit

Hi all — engineering findings and recommended remediation below.

Root cause (short):
- On 2027-02-08 at ~02:55 UTC we ran a backfill job to backfill late-arriving telemetry for FastRetail (job id: backfill-fr-20270208, GH commit: b7e4c9f). The backfill worker failed to include the dedupe_key header in a small subset of events when re-emitting to the ingestion topic. That caused the ingestion pipeline to surface those events as new sessions rather than suppressed duplicates.

Evidence:
- We compared producer offsets and found re-emitted events with identical prompt_hash + client_session_id but with no dedupe_key present. Sample rows included in engineer-rootcause-report.pdf.

Impact & numbers:
- Confirmed extra tokens: 1,217,640 (close to Ben's estimate).
- Affected timeframe: 2027-02-08 02:55 UTC — 2027-02-09 12:30 UTC (auto-scaling exaggerated the spike).

Remediation and ask:
- Proposed credit amount: $1,420 (we adjust for a small margin after removing one-off internal test traffic).
- We will issue a formal credit note and amend the Feb invoice prior to Feb 16 finance cut.
- Root-cause fix: backfill worker now sets dedupe_key and we've added a unit test to prevent regressions (PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/backfill/pull/412).

Priya — I'm happy to jump on a quick call to walk through the evidence (I can share the CSV extracts and the commit). If you accept the proposed credit, billing will prepare the credit note and notify your finance contact.

Apologies for the disruption — we'll also add an automated alert to detect anomalous duplicate session rates going forward.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Software Engineer, Ingest & Telemetry
Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
